source_issues.detail: src_1 (AoPS wiki, IMO 2022 P6) and src_2 (Evan Chen IMO 2022 notes) are cited with empty excerpts and explicitly as 'context only'. I could not retrieve them (no browsing) and do not treat them as checked; they are not load-bearing: every lemma used is re-proved in §0–§1, so no result is taken on citation. No misattribution: the candidate does not claim to have used any theorem from them.

src_3 (problema-2/submission/parte-1.md) is an internal repo file not included in the envelope. The candidate restates its Lemmas with proofs, so the proof does not depend on reading it. If the orchestrator wants a citation trail, attach the file or its excerpt.

computation_issues.detail: Python interpreter version is not recorded (scripts use only the standard library; orchestrator re-runs succeeded with python3). Reported wall-clock (0.24s/0.39s) differs slightly from trusted re-runs (0.47s/0.71s) — immaterial, both far below the 10-minute limit. code_2, code_4, code_6, code_7 import the shared module code_1 as `conta_cammini`; the artifact bundle must keep that filename for reproduction.

code_6 (200k random labellings) and code_7 (annealing, 8 seeds all reaching 88) are correctly labelled as evidence only and are not used in the proof. Note the annealing optimum with 5 valleys and 88 paths corresponds to X=3, |H|=1, i=2, q=13, which is consistent with Lemma 7 (4q = 47+5 = 52).

rule_violations.detail: The rules supplied are the team's internal defaults (CLAUDE.md), not the official competition regulation. Points that depend on the real regulation: (a) admissibility of a computer-assisted lower bound with a written reduction (currently allowed: allow_computation=true, reduction to (★) is proved in §2, coverage declared, exact integer arithmetic, <1s runtime); (b) whether node counts/wall-clock must be reported in a specific format; (c) whether the submitted labelling format (32 comma-separated 0/1 strings, coordinate 1 on the left) matches the checker's expected coordinate convention (irrelevant for the value, which is what is scored). Please supply the official rules to close these.

claim_provenance.notes: Lower bound: hand case analysis (§1–§2) reduces T<=87 to predicate (★); (★) is refuted by two independent exhaustive exact checks whose outputs (1377/27540/0 and 3672/73440/0) the orchestrator reproduced. The predicate tested by the scripts is exactly (★) (independent 12-set, every u outside, forest test = edges = vertices - components / union-find). Symmetry reduction (XOR translations, transitive, preserve independence and acyclicity) is justified and cross-validated by the unreduced run. Upper bound: explicit labelling, bijection asserted, 88 reproduced by recursion and by explicit DFS. Correctness of the algebra in Lemmas 5–7 and the case split was spot-checked only insofar as needed to confirm the computation is applied to the right finite set; full mathematical review is Referee A's remit.

report.reproducibility_notes: All seven artifacts were re-run by the orchestrator from a clean copy: code_2 (0.5s) and code_3 (0.7s) reproduce the exact counts claimed in the proof text with 0 acyclic complements; code_4 and code_5 both print 88 with the same 8 valleys and the same 32-vertex order as in §4; code_6 confirms the identity on 200k random labellings; code_7 reaches 88 on all 8 seeds (79s). Standard-library Python only, integer arithmetic throughout; total verification time for the proof-relevant scripts (code_2..code_5) is under 2 seconds, far below the 10-minute limit. Certificates are independently checkable: the two lower-bound scripts use genuinely different enumeration (backtracking with symmetry vs. bipartite bitmask scan) and different acyclicity tests.
